entries.title: Shared/Core update: compaction-summary
entries.summary: Shared/Core, Agent Runtime changes across 3 file(s) (+65/−9).

ai.title: Conversation summary accepts translated section headings
ai.summary: The agent runtime conversation summary now recognizes model replies that translate the format's section headings into another language, fixing a failure where valid summaries were discarded. The mechanism is a new `summaryFromReply` helper that counts markdown headings when the English `## Objective` marker is missing, using `MIN_TRANSLATED_SECTIONS` to determine if the reply has the correct structure. The `compaction-summary.ts` prompt instructions are updated to require English headings explicitly, and a new 'unrecognized' error kind distinguishes structurally invalid replies from empty ones. Two additional changes are included: the Axiom-only log allowlist documents the new error kind, and the prompt's language rule is tightened.
ai.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/conversation-summary.ts`, the new `summaryFromReply` function accepts replies with at least `MIN_TRANSLATED_SECTIONS` (6) markdown headings even when the English '## Objective' header is absent, and `SummaryError` gains an 'unrecognized' kind for non-empty replies that fail to meet that threshold.

changes.what: Adds `summaryFromReply` which validates translated summaries and distinguishes 'unrecognized' from 'empty' errors
Modifies the compaction summary prompt to enforce English headings while allowing translated body text
Updates the Axiom-only log comment for `COMPACTION_SUMMARY_FIELDS` to include the new 'unrecognized' error kind

eli5.text: The AI assistant now accepts its own summary notes even when the headings are in a language other than English, preventing it from discarding valid summaries that were correctly translated. This improves the reliability of long coding sessions for anyone who works with the assistant in a language other than English. You do not need to take any action, but you may notice the assistant remembering your work more consistently after long pauses.
